subtype: Laughing to fit in or mask [Regulating]
passage: At lunch, a group of boys began imitating the new boy's accent. Everyone laughed, and Dolma laughed too, a bit too loudly. I was sitting across from her and noticed her laugh stopped at her mouth. Her eyes were on her tray. When the joke was repeated, she looked down and picked at her rice. I'm Sahil, and I can't say what was in her mind. Maybe she found it funny. Maybe she didn't. But when the group moved on, she said quietly, "I shouldn't have laughed." I said, "You didn't have to." She nodded.

qa.q: What did the group of boys imitate at lunch?
qa.a: They imitated the new boy's accent.

qa.q: What might Dolma have felt when she laughed too loudly, and what else could it be?
qa.a: She may have been uneasy and laughing to fit in, since her laugh stopped at her mouth and she said she shouldn't have laughed. Sahil admits she might also have found it funny.

qa.q: What could Dolma do next time a joke feels unkind?
qa.a: She can stay quiet or say calmly, "that's not funny," and sit with safer friends. Sahil's reply shows she doesn't have to laugh.

qa.q: How might the new boy have felt when everyone laughed?
qa.a: He probably felt singled out and hurt. He may not have known which laughs were real.

grounding: A teenager laughs along with a group joke that feels unkind, masking unease, and an observer notices.

subtype: Laughing to fit in or mask [Regulating]
passage:
Monday: In the canteen, Vasudha laughed along when the others mocked Pooja's haircut. Pooja laughed too, though her eyes stayed flat. 
Wednesday: Pooja sat alone. Vasudha noticed and remembered the flat eyes. She felt her stomach turn.
Friday: Vasudha walked over. "I laughed on Monday and I shouldn't have. It wasn't funny." Pooja looked up. "I hated it. I laughed to fit in." "Me too," said Vasudha. "Next time I'll say 'that's not funny'." Pooja smiled, a real one this time. "Then I'll sit with you at lunch."

qa.q: On which day did Vasudha laugh along in the canteen?
What was Pooja feeling when she laughed with flat eyes on Monday?
qa.a: She felt hurt and laughed to fit in. Her flat eyes and later sitting alone show it wasn't real amusement.

qa.q: What could Vasudha do differently the next time someone is mocked?
qa.a: She can say "that's not funny" calmly and sit with someone kind. That protects the boundary and the friendship.

qa.q: How does Vasudha see her own laugh by Friday?
qa.a: She regrets it and feels uneasy. Seeing Pooja's flat eyes made her realise it hurt.

grounding: A teenager hides hurt behind a laugh to fit in, and later a friend names a calm boundary.
